name: Strategic individual-tree planting
reason: Deliberately sited single tree addressing a defined local heat problem; distinct from an isolated existing tree, which the document disqualifies.

name: Tree cluster
reason: Overlapping canopies produce a continuous shaded microclimate distinct from the same trees dispersed; different soil-volume and spacing requirements.

name: Tree grove
reason: Document distinguishes a grove from a cluster as a composed collective structure forming a defined shaded room for occupation.

name: Conventional individual tree pit
reason: Distinct and near-universal physical detail, but the document calls it a minimum planting provision rather than a preferred NbS typology.

name: Enlarged tree pit
reason: Substantially greater rooting volume gives different tree longevity, water storage and failure behaviour than a conventional pit.

name: Structural-soil tree pit
reason: Engineered soil-and-stone medium under paving is a distinct substrate with its own specification, usable-volume limits and installation risks.

name: Suspended-pavement or soil-cell tree pit
reason: Load-bearing frame over uncompacted soil is a different construction and maintenance system from structural soil, with different cost and utility constraints.

name: Stormwater tree pit
reason: Deliberate hydrological connection to adjacent runoff makes it a distinct system; the document calls it more accurately an NbS than a conventional pit.

name: Bioretention tree pit
reason: Engineered filter media, storage zones and underdrainage give clogging, sediment and maintenance behaviour genuinely different from a basic stormwater pit.

name: Connected tree pits
reason: Same physical system as a continuous tree trench — a shared uninterrupted below-ground soil volume; only the surface expression differs.

name: Continuous tree trench
reason: Canonical continuous below-ground rooting volume serving a sequence of trees; also functions as a stormwater conveyance and storage structure.

name: Continuous open planting bed for trees
reason: Visible unpaved connected soil strip; surface permeability and soil exposure differ from a buried trench under pavement.

name: Connected multi-layer planting bed
reason: Several vegetation layers give higher evapotranspiration, habitat and maintenance complexity than the tree-only strip in A12.

name: Tree island
reason: Planted island interrupting a large paved or trafficked surface; distinct form and size-dependent performance.

name: Parking-lot tree island
reason: Same physical system as a tree island; parking is a location context that A14 already lists, not a distinct typology.

name: Conventional planting bed
reason: Physically distinct, but is effectively the umbrella of B2–B4 and the document says a decorative bed is not automatically NbS.

name: Shrub-dominated planting bed
reason: Shrub layer gives ground-level shading and road/building buffering where trees are impossible; distinct visibility and safety constraints.

name: Herbaceous perennial bed
reason: Canonical perennial planting system; distinct vegetation structure, seasonal cover and maintenance regime from shrub or groundcover beds.

name: Groundcover planting
reason: Continuous low soil cover replacing gravel, bare soil or mown turf; distinct surface-temperature and soil-moisture behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: reduced surface heating + soil moisture retention

name: Pollinator bed
reason: Physically a herbaceous perennial bed; differs only by species-selection objective, which the document treats as an ecological layer within other typologies.

name: Pocket meadow
reason: Meadow community with low-frequency cutting is a distinct vegetation and management system, not an ornamental perennial bed.

name: Rain garden
reason: Shallow ground-connected planted depression storing and infiltrating runoff; the document calls it a genuine small-scale NbS.

name: Bioswale
reason: Linear conveyance function, check dams and longitudinal space requirements distinguish it from the discrete rain-garden basin.

name: Infiltration planting bed
reason: Hydraulically connected but undepressed and without engineered filter layers or underdrainage; different siting constraints from bioretention.

name: Depressed bioretention bed
reason: Engineered media, storage volume and overflow give different failure and maintenance behaviour from a simple rain garden.

name: Vegetated planter with stormwater function
reason: Explicitly distinguished from an ordinary decorative container by hydraulic connection; enables retrofit where ground infiltration is impossible.

name: Large-volume connected planters
reason: Connected large planters create a continuous vegetated edge with shared rooting volume where excavation is impossible; distinct from single stormwater planters.

name: Mobile planter
reason: Document classifies movable containers as temporary green infrastructure, not NbS; ordinary planters are an explicitly disqualified enabling component.

name: Extensive green roof
reason: Shallow substrate, stress-tolerant vegetation and low structural load form a distinct roof system with limited street-level cooling.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration + surface albedo at roof level

name: Semi-intensive green roof
reason: Intermediate substrate depth supports wider vegetation and water storage with different structural and irrigation demands from extensive roofs.

name: Intensive green roof
reason: Deep growing medium supporting lawns, shrubs and trees; distinct structural load, drainage and maintenance regime.

name: Roof garden
reason: Document states a roof garden is usually an intensive or semi-intensive roof, distinguished by human use rather than a different physical system.

name: Biodiverse green roof
reason: Varied substrate depths, mineral materials and microhabitats form a physically different roof build-up from a standardised planting mat.

name: Brown roof
reason: Locally characteristic nutrient-poor substrate and open heterogeneous habitat is a distinct substrate specification, though it overlaps biodiverse roofs.

name: Blue roof
reason: Explicitly disqualified: a non-vegetated blue roof is blue infrastructure or an NbS-supporting component, not an NbS; C8 covers the vegetated case.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from stored water only; no vegetation

name: Blue-green roof
reason: Canonical vegetated roof with dedicated water storage feeding plants; integrates stormwater, evapotranspiration and habitat in one build-up.

name: Retention green roof
reason: Document says it differs from a blue-green roof only where a methodology needs separate technical categories; in practice the terms overlap.

name: Detention green roof
reason: Same physical system as a vegetated roof with controlled storage; peak-flow delay is a hydraulic setting, not a distinct physical form.

name: Biosolar roof
reason: Coordinated PV-and-vegetation build-up with panel spacing, substrate and access designed together; the NbS-qualifying form of the solar-green roof.

name: Solar-green roof
reason: Same physical system (PV plus vegetation); the document separates them only by ecological design intent, so the NbS-qualifying entry is canonical.

name: Productive green roof
reason: Edible planting with raised beds, deeper substrate and nutrient and irrigation management is a distinct roof system from ornamental green roofs.

name: Rooftop farm
reason: Distinct in scale and management intensity from a productive roof, but the document says it is not automatically NbS unless ecological conditions are met.

name: Roof meadow
reason: Meadow community needs more varied substrate and moisture than a sedum roof and a mowing regime; distinct build-up and management.

name: Roof wetland
reason: Wetland vegetation with controlled standing water on a roof is a specialised hydraulic and waterproofing system with strong evaporative cooling.

name: Tree roof or rooftop woodland
reason: Multiple trees on a roof demand soil depth, anchoring and wind assessment beyond an intensive roof, with different failure behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade + evapotranspiration at roof level

name: Direct ground-rooted green facade
reason: Self-clinging plants on the wall surface with no support frame; lowest technical complexity and distinct facade-maintenance implications.

name: Indirect ground-rooted green facade
reason: Canonical ground-rooted system on a separate support with an air gap; the gap changes facade protection and ventilation behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: facade shading + evapotranspiration + ventilated air gap

name: Ground-rooted cable facade
reason: Document names it a subtype of the indirect facade; cable is one of the support options D2 already lists.

name: Ground-rooted mesh or trellis facade
reason: Support-material variant of the indirect ground-rooted facade, which explicitly includes mesh and trellis panels; same rooting and irrigation system.

name: Planter-rooted green facade
reason: Rooting in planters at multiple levels creates irrigation dependency and failure sensitivity genuinely different from ground-rooted facades.

name: Cascading facade planting
reason: Trailing growth downward from elevated planters is a distinct physical arrangement with its own container, drainage and access constraints.

name: Modular living wall
reason: Canonical living wall: modular panels fixed to a support structure with integrated irrigation and drainage; rapid coverage, pump-failure risk.

name: Substrate-based living wall
reason: Substrate buffering of water and nutrients gives different weight, drying and failure behaviour, but it overlaps the modular wall in D7.

name: Hydroponic living wall
reason: Soil-free inert medium with fully engineered nutrient delivery; dependence on mechanical systems and skilled maintenance is distinct from substrate walls.

name: Felt-pocket living wall
reason: Document names it a subtype of the hydroponic or low-substrate wall; same irrigation dependency and drying failure mode.

name: Vegetated screen
reason: Freestanding vertical vegetated structure not part of a facade; used for shade, privacy, wind and glare control.

name: Green noise barrier
reason: Acoustic structure combined with vegetation; distinct construction, siting along transport corridors and soil-connection requirements.

name: Vegetated retaining wall
reason: Load-retaining structure with integrated planting cells, terraces or pockets; vegetation stabilises surfaces and reduces exposed mineral heating.

name: Green gabion wall
reason: D13 explicitly lists gabions as one of its construction variants; same physical system and planting-and-water strategy requirement.

name: Moss wall
reason: Explicitly disqualified: preserved moss is not living and provides negligible ecosystem function; outdoor living moss has restricted applicability.
cooling_mechanism: none — negligible; minor humidity if living

name: Green pergola
reason: Canonical overhead frame carrying climbers above an occupied space; delivers shade before or instead of mature tree canopy.

name: Vine-covered shade structure
reason: Same physical system as a green pergola — a frame carrying a climbing-plant canopy; differs only in stated design emphasis and support material.

name: Vegetated arcade
reason: Linear repeated-bay covered route giving continuous pedestrian shade along a corridor; distinct geometry from a discrete pergola.

name: Vegetated canopy
reason: A freestanding overhead support carrying climbing or trailing vegetation is the same physical system as a green pergola.

name: Green bus stop
reason: Document presents the waiting shelter as the broader category; transport is a location context, not a distinct physical shelter type.

name: Green waiting shelter
reason: Canonical vegetated shelter providing shaded thermal refuge at stops, schools, markets and interchanges; qualifies where vegetation is real and managed.

name: Street with Individual Trees
reason: Document binding: "Street Trees" must be removed as a street-scale typology; it is an element (A4-A15) already defined at element scale, not an integrated linear system.

name: Tree Avenue
reason: Canonical integrated linear canopy system: continuous connected tree-soil rows (A10-A13) producing a continuous shaded corridor. Distinct form, distinct cooling behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: shade — continuous linear canopy, plus evapotranspiration

name: Double Tree Avenue
reason: Same system, same elements (A10-A13), same mechanism; only canopy density differs. Row count is an intensity parameter (canopy cover input), not a separate typology.
cooling_mechanism: shade — continuous linear canopy at higher density

name: Green Boulevard
reason: Defined by full integration of canopy, ground-level vegetation, permeable surfaces and stormwater — that is the Green Street definition. Corridor width is a parameter, not a typology.

name: Green Street
reason: The canonical comprehensive street-scale system: vegetation, engineered soils, bioretention and public-realm improvement coordinated across the right-of-way.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration + evaporation from bioretention + permeability

name: Complete Green Street
reason: Document states the "complete" aspect refers to transport functionality, not ecology; its NbS content is explicitly Green Street elements. No distinct cooling behaviour.

name: Living Street
reason: A traffic-regulation and street-design model (low speed, public-life priority); vegetation is optional infill. Its NbS content is a package of Green Street and pedestrian-street entries.

name: Shared Street
reason: Document states NbS are supporting elements rather than the defining characteristic; shared-surface is a traffic-management model. Cooling content already captured by Green Street.

name: Green Median
reason: Canonical linear vegetated strip within the carriageway cross-section: de-sealed, plantable, often bioretentive. Distinct retrofittable form with its own cooling behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration + reduced impervious heat storage; shade where trees

name: Green Verge
reason: Physically identical to a green median — continuous vegetated strip in the right-of-way with the same element palette; only its position in the cross-section differs.

name: Bioswale Street
reason: Explicitly "a Green Street in which bioswales dominate"; defined by which element (B8) is emphasised. Per the document, elements should be referenced, not redefined as typologies.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation and infiltration from swales + shade

name: Rain Garden Street
reason: Explicitly "a Green Street" with B7 repeated along the corridor; a dominant-element variant of the same system, distinguished only from 2.11 by discrete versus linear retention.

name: Green Tram Corridor
reason: Genuinely distinct linear system: vegetation replaces ballast and asphalt within the rail alignment, a de-sealing typology with no pedestrian shade component.
cooling_mechanism: surface albedo/permeability + evapotranspiration from de-sealed track bed

name: Green Cycle Corridor
reason: Same physical system as a green pedestrian street — a vegetated car-free corridor under continuous canopy; its components are wholly borrowed. Differs only by user mode.

name: Green Pedestrian Street
reason: Distinct system: no carriageway, so vegetation occupies the full width as primary infrastructure, giving canopy geometry and receptor exposure unlike any trafficked street.
cooling_mechanism: shade — full-width canopy over the pedestrian surface + evapotranspiration

name: Green Alley
reason: Distinct constrained system: high aspect ratio, little ground connection, cooling delivered mainly through vertical greening and permeable resurfacing rather than canopy.

name: Green Parking Lane
reason: Distinct modular retrofit of the parking bay: intermittent tree islands and bioretention pockets that de-seal carriageway edge while retaining parking. Not a continuous strip.
cooling_mechanism: shade over parked vehicles and pavement + permeability and evaporation

name: Tree Plaza
reason: Document names it a clearly defined public-space typology: canopy organises the whole square. Distinct spatial structure and strong direct shade benefit.
cooling_mechanism: shade — canopy over gathering and seating areas + evapotranspiration

name: Cooling Plaza
reason: Document names it a valid public-space typology; combination of tree canopy, vegetated overhead structures and water-sensitive planting is a recognisable heat-refuge configuration.
cooling_mechanism: shade (trees plus vegetated structures) + evapotranspiration and evaporation

name: Permeable Plaza
reason: Document names it a valid typology; defined by de-sealing and infiltration rather than shade, so its cooling behaviour is genuinely distinct from tree and cooling plazas.
cooling_mechanism: surface permeability and evaporation + reduced heat storage

name: Civic Green
reason: Document names it a valid typology; replacing a hard civic surface with a substantial green ground plane is a distinct form with distinct cooling behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from green ground plane + reduced imperviousness

name: Courtyard Greening
reason: Distinct enclosed-geometry system with restricted air movement and high radiant load; already an approved v1.1 typology (courtyard_greening).
cooling_mechanism: facade and ground shading + evapotranspiration in an enclosed volume

name: Schoolyard Greening
reason: Document calls it a land-use context, but it is an approved literature-grounded v1.1 typology and the gating rules select it directly; dropping it breaks them. Author must rule.
cooling_mechanism: shade over play surfaces + evapotranspiration + de-sealing

name: Hospital Landscape
reason: Document: a land-use context, already captured by the tool's land_use input; physically it is a tree/cooling plaza plus paths. But gating rules expect it selectable — author must rule.

name: Campus Landscape
reason: Document: a land-use context; also a multi-scale package of kept entries (green streets, avenues, rain gardens, roofs), not one typology. Gating rules expect it — author must rule.

name: Market Square Greening
reason: A cooling plaza serving a market: perimeter canopy and vegetated shade structures over densely occupied paving. The market use is an operational constraint, not a distinct form.
cooling_mechanism: shade over stalls and occupied paving + evapotranspiration

name: Memorial Landscape
reason: Document: a land-use context captured by land_use; its physical content is tree groves, meadows and rain gardens already kept. Gating rules expect it selectable — author must rule.

name: Green Public Courtyard
reason: Its own text distinguishes it by public access, social use and management — ownership and access attributes, not physical form or cooling behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: facade and ground shading + evapotranspiration in an enclosed volume

name: Green Transport Forecourt
reason: A cooling plaza at an interchange: shading waiting zones and pedestrian flows. Defined by the adjacent land use, not by a distinct spatial or climatic structure.
cooling_mechanism: shade over waiting zones and pedestrian flows + evapotranspiration

name: Green Cultural Forecourt
reason: A tree plaza in a cultural setting; representational and visibility constraints follow from the adjacent building, not from a different physical or cooling system.
cooling_mechanism: shade — canopy over gathering space + evapotranspiration

name: Cooling Refuge
reason: Its own text says the defining criterion is its role in a heat-health strategy, not its form; physically it is a small cooling plaza with the same components.
cooling_mechanism: shade — dense canopy and vegetated structures + evaporation

name: Green Playground
reason: Same physical system as schoolyard greening — de-sealed, shaded, vegetated play landscape; differs only in institutional setting. Becomes canonical if 3.6 is dropped as a context.
cooling_mechanism: shade over play surfaces + evapotranspiration + de-sealing

name: Pocket Park
reason: Size-axis typology with distinct constrained form; already the tool's pocket_park, canonical smallest park tier.

name: Neighbourhood Park
reason: Size/service-area tier with distinct extent and vegetation share; supports a measurable park cool-island beyond a pocket park.

name: Community Park
reason: Document states the distinguishing feature is social ownership, not size or form; physically a neighbourhood park, governance is an attribute.

name: District Park
reason: Size tier large enough for multiple habitat types and documented influence on surrounding microclimate; distinct from neighbourhood scale.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration, cool-air export to surroundings

name: Regional Park
reason: Top tier of the size axis; distinct behaviour through cool-air-mass generation and regional connectivity rather than site-scale shading.

name: Cooling Park
reason: Document says its defining characteristic is performance, not form; it is the thermal objective the tool's park_upgrade already expresses.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration + low-heat surfaces (objective, not a form)

name: Biodiversity Park
reason: Defined by ecological objective; its physical form is the naturalistic park's habitat mosaic, with no separate cooling behaviour.

name: Forest Park
reason: A tree-dominated park is the site-scale urban forest under public access; duplicates the woodland-scale entry rather than adding a park tier.

name: Therapeutic Park
reason: User-programme category, not a form; a health-programme and user-group attribute. Its shade and sensory planting are already kept elements.

name: Inclusive Park
reason: Accessibility and equity attribute applicable to every park typology; no distinct physical form or cooling behaviour.

name: Water Park
reason: Permanent water bodies form the dominant substrate, giving evaporative cooling absent from vegetation-only parks; document's ecological reading, not the aquatic facility.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from open water + riparian shade

name: Adventure Park
reason: Play-programme category; its landform, woodland and shaded clearings are existing elements, and it has no distinct cooling behaviour.

name: Sports Park
reason: Recreation land-use programme; NbS content is perimeter tree belts and bioswales already catalogued, and exposed pitches remain thermally stressful.

name: Botanical Garden
reason: Institutional land-use context defined by collections, research and curation; cooling is that of a well-treed park, captured by land_use.

name: Naturalistic Park
reason: Distinct form of multi-layer spontaneous vegetation, meadow and successional woodland replacing mown lawn; canonical entry for biodiversity and restoration parks.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from tall multi-layer vegetation + shade

name: Floodable Park
reason: Same multifunctional detention landscape as the stormwater park, differing only in inundation frequency; document treats stormwater park as the broader case.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation when inundated + evapotranspiration when dry

name: Stormwater Park
reason: Canonical detention-landscape park; runoff storage and treatment give a distinct intermittent-moisture cooling regime, unlike a permanent water park.

name: Productive Park
reason: Food production is a land-use and production category per the document's urban agriculture ruling; orchards and food forests are separate elements.
cooling_mechanism: none distinct (varies from orchard canopy to bare beds)

name: Ecological Restoration Park
reason: Defined by site history and delivery process, not form; the outcome is a naturalistic park, with brownfield/landfill status a site-condition input.

name: Linear Park
reason: Distinct elongated form that distributes cooling along the urban fabric and aids ventilation; a park typology, not the tool's blue_green_corridor.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration distributed along a corridor; ventilation path

name: River Park
reason: A linear park aligned on a watercourse; its riparian ecology is already covered by the tool's riparian_restoration and blue_green_corridor.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from watercourse + riparian canopy shade

name: Coastal Park
reason: Distinct dune, mangrove and shoreline form with context-gated availability; cooling regime governed by sea breeze and saline substrates.

name: Heritage Park
reason: Conservation context and design constraint rather than a form; belongs in a site-constraint input that limits which interventions are permitted.

name: Urban Forest
reason: CREATION: kept only as meaning 2, a site-scale tree-dominated intervention matching the tool's urban_forest; the citywide tree-resource meaning is a strategy and excluded.

name: Community Woodland
reason: CREATION or RESTORATION depending on site; defined by stewardship and participation rather than woodland form, so governance becomes an attribute.

name: Microforest
reason: CREATION: canonical small dense woodland patch; high planting density on a constrained site gives rapid, spatially local canopy cooling.

name: Miyawaki-style Forest
reason: CREATION: the document rules it a subtype of microforest defined by planting method, not a separate typology.

name: Pocket Woodland
reason: CREATION (may retain existing trees): same small woodland patch as microforest, differing only in planting density and method; cooling behaviour equivalent.

name: Riparian Forest
reason: CREATION or RESTORATION: same hydrologically driven woodland the tool already carries as riparian_restoration; keeping both would duplicate one system.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade over water + high evapotranspiration from moist soils

name: Climate Forest
reason: Neither creation nor restoration: the document rules it a management and design objective; becomes a species-and-resilience attribute on kept woodland typologies.
cooling_mechanism: none distinct (objective applied to other woodland forms)

name: Native Woodland
reason: Neither creation nor restoration: an ecological-composition attribute per the document's own classification note; cooling matches any woodland of equal structure.

name: Native Forest Restoration
reason: RESTORATION: the document states degraded woodland restoration is the broader category; native focus is a composition attribute of the same intervention.

name: Degraded Woodland Restoration
reason: RESTORATION: canonical intervention on existing woodland, gated on woodland already being present; distinct from establishing new woodland.
cooling_mechanism: restored canopy shade + evapotranspiration from repaired soils

name: Forest Expansion
reason: CREATION: physically new woodland establishment on adjoining non-forest land; adjacency to an existing patch is a siting attribute, not a form.
cooling_mechanism: new canopy shade + evapotranspiration; reduced edge exposure

name: Woodland Edge Restoration
reason: RESTORATION: listed by 5.10 itself as one of its typical interventions; a graduated mantle is a component of restoring existing woodland.
cooling_mechanism: wind buffering + evapotranspiration from shrub layer

name: Understory Enrichment
reason: RESTORATION: an element-scale planting action named within 5.10's own intervention list; not a standalone woodland typology.
cooling_mechanism: increased evapotranspiration + ground shading beneath canopy

name: Canopy Diversification
reason: RESTORATION: species and age-class enrichment of existing woodland, equivalent to 5.10's canopy gap planting; adds resilience, not a distinct form.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade continuity over time (marginal short-term gain)

name: Afforestation
reason: CREATION: canonical establishment of woodland on land not recently forested; availability gated on non-forested, ecologically suitable land.
cooling_mechanism: new canopy shade + evapotranspiration (long lead time)

name: Reforestation
reason: RESTORATION: re-establishment on previously forested land, gated on land history and residual seed bank; distinct from afforestation on that gate alone.

name: Assisted Natural Regeneration
reason: RESTORATION: a delivery method that 5.16 explicitly names as one of its own routes; produces no distinct woodland form.

name: Urban Woodland Buffer
reason: CREATION: distinct linear belt sited between heat-generating and sensitive land uses; buffering and screening behaviour differs from patch woodland.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade + evapotranspiration; wind and heat-source buffering

name: Constructed Wetland
reason: Engineered wetland with distinct physical form and strong evaporative cooling; the rules name it explicitly as a valid composite typology.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation + evapotranspiration from open water and emergent vegetation

name: Retention Pond
reason: Constructed permanent water body with littoral planting; distinct from detention basin by permanent pool and continuous evaporative cooling.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from permanent open water + marginal vegetation evapotranspiration

name: Detention Basin
reason: Constructed dry basin, distinct form; but document notes cooling is episodic and biodiversity limited, so cooling relevance is marginal.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from grassed/planted basin, episodic (only when wet)

name: Water Square
reason: Distinct dual-function hard public space with terraced storage; document notes limited ecological value unless heavily vegetated, echoing the blue-roof caveat.
cooling_mechanism: episodic evaporation + surface permeability; vegetated shade only if planted

name: Daylighted Stream
reason: Distinct hydrological intervention (culvert removal) creating new surface water plus riparian vegetation; not a restoration of an existing open channel.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from restored channel + shade and evapotranspiration from riparian planting

name: Stream Restoration
reason: Same restoration process as river restoration (bank naturalisation, meanders, floodplain reconnection); differs only in watercourse scale, an attribute not a typology.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from open channel + riparian shade and evapotranspiration

name: River Restoration
reason: Canonical watercourse-restoration typology; distinct physical works on an existing open channel and its banks, with clear cooling behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from open water + riparian shade and evapotranspiration

name: Canal Restoration
reason: Distinct from river restoration: engineered vertical-walled waterway restored via edge planting, floating wetlands and habitat shelves rather than morphology.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from water surface + edge vegetation evapotranspiration

name: Floodable Park
reason: The entry is itself only a cross-reference to Section 4.16; the park-scale entry should be canonical and available at water-landscape scale.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from park vegetation + episodic evaporation when flooded

name: Floodplain Restoration
reason: Distinct lateral intervention (levee setback, regrading, secondary channels) on the floodplain rather than the channel; large area, high cooling potential.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from wet meadow and riparian woodland + evaporation from wetted floodplain

name: Urban Lake Restoration
reason: Distinct still-water restoration (shoreline naturalisation, habitat islands, sediment management); large permanent water surface gives strong evaporative cooling.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from large open water surface + shoreline vegetation evapotranspiration

name: Living Shoreline
reason: Distinct soft bank-protection system replacing hard engineering; document states it maintains natural coastal OR freshwater processes, so lake shores qualify alongside sea.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from marsh vegetation; cooling secondary to erosion control

name: Floating Wetland
reason: Discrete built planted platform deployable where shoreline restoration is impossible; distinct form from constructed wetland, needs an existing water body of depth.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from wetland planting + shading of the water surface

name: Riparian Buffer
reason: Discrete vegetated strip beside a watercourse; document distinguishes it from riparian forest (5.6) by allowing grass, shrub or mixed vegetation.
cooling_mechanism: shade over water and bank + evapotranspiration

name: Urban Sponge Landscape
reason: Document states it is not a single intervention but combines rain gardens, wetlands, ponds, basins and permeable surfaces: a package of kept entries.
cooling_mechanism: none directly — inherits cooling from its component typologies

name: Green Corridor
reason: Multifunctional terrestrial linear system named in the rules as a valid composite; distributes cooling and mobility through the urban fabric.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration along a continuous vegetated route

name: Ecological Corridor
reason: Canonical habitat-driven corridor: low disturbance, species-appropriate vegetation, limited public access — physically distinct from the public-realm green corridor.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration; cooling secondary to connectivity

name: Pollinator Corridor
reason: Target-species variant of an ecological corridor; the document's own note makes target function a separate attribute, not an equivalent typology.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from flowering beds and meadow strips; minimal

name: Blue-Green Corridor
reason: Distinct combined terrestrial-aquatic linear system; already a literature-grounded v1.1 tool typology, so it is the canonical aquatic-medium corridor.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from water + evapotranspiration and shade from corridor vegetation

name: River Corridor
reason: Distinct from blue-green corridor: organised around an existing river with lateral bank-floodplain connection; strong cooling and ventilation potential.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from river + riparian shade + cool-air channelling along the valley

name: Railway Green Corridor
reason: Distinct physical context (embankments, trackside pioneer and brownfield habitat, operational constraints); depends on an existing active or former rail alignment.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from trackside and embankment vegetation + shade where woodland strips exist

name: Green Wedge
reason: Metropolitan-scale open-land planning structure containing forests, agriculture, parks and wetlands; a growth-management model, not a discrete intervention.
cooling_mechanism: regional ventilation / cool-air advection toward dense districts

name: Habitat Stepping Stones
reason: The document names it a fragmented-connectivity strategy; it is a spacing pattern of already-kept entries (pocket parks, green roofs, rain gardens, pocket meadows).
cooling_mechanism: none directly — distributed shade and evapotranspiration from its component patches

name: Ecological Network
reason: The document calls it a complete citywide system of cores, corridors and stepping stones: a metropolitan planning framework packaging kept typologies.
cooling_mechanism: none directly — network-scale distribution of component cooling

name: Habitat Corridor
reason: Document states it is 'more specific than a general ecological corridor'; a target-species specification of the same corridor form.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration depending on target vegetation

name: Woodland Corridor
reason: Vegetation-structure variant of an ecological corridor; but its canopy gives materially stronger shade cooling than a generic corridor, so ruling needed.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade + evapotranspiration; strongest cooling of the corridor variants

name: Wetland Corridor
reason: A connected sequence of wetlands, ponds, swales and riparian areas is the aquatic-medium case already covered by the blue-green corridor.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation from water + evapotranspiration from wetland vegetation

name: Meadow Corridor
reason: Grassland vegetation-structure variant of an ecological corridor; composed of pocket meadows and park meadow systems already defined elsewhere.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from grassland; no shade, weak cooling

name: Coastal Ecological Corridor
reason: Distinct physical form (dunes, mangroves, coastal wetlands, estuarine habitat) and distinct coastal cooling and erosion-resilience behaviour.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from coastal vegetation + sea-breeze penetration inland

name: Urban Ecological Spine
reason: A city-scale structuring axis assembled from parks, streets, rivers, rail corridors and woodland; a planning designation over kept corridor typologies.
cooling_mechanism: none directly — aggregate of its component corridors

name: Green Belt
reason: Document states its function is growth control and that it should not automatically be classified as an ecological network; a land-use designation.
cooling_mechanism: regional evapotranspiration and cool-air supply; no site-scale form

name: Ecological Buffer
reason: Document calls it a supporting component, not a network; defined by protective function with no distinct vegetation form of its own.
cooling_mechanism: shade + evapotranspiration of whatever planting realises it; not distinct

name: Community Garden
reason: Canonical productive-garden composite: beds, fruit trees, composting and water harvesting form one coherent, distinctly cooling planted system.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration, with limited shade from fruit trees

name: Allotment Garden
reason: Distinct plot-subdivided form with sheds and boundary hedges, but the document lists it as a governance model rather than a physical typology.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration; reduced by sheds, paths and paving

name: Urban Orchard
reason: Fruit- and nut-tree stand with flowering understory is a distinct physical form combining canopy shade with production.

name: Food Forest
reason: Multi-layered woodland-mimicking structure gives it a physical form and cooling behaviour distinct from orchards and gardens.
cooling_mechanism: layered canopy shade plus high evapotranspiration

name: Urban Farm
reason: Canonical field-scale production site; larger cultivated ground plane and infrastructure distinguish it physically from garden-scale entries.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from cultivated ground; little shade

name: Urban Agriculture
reason: Document states it is a broad land-use and production category, not one typology; it is an umbrella over kept entries 8.1-8.5.

name: Rooftop Agriculture
reason: Entry is itself only a cross-reference to C13 Productive Green Roof and C14 Rooftop Farm; merge into the canonical roof entries.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration and reduced roof heat gain

name: Vertical Farming
reason: Document states vertical farming should not normally be classified as NbS; it is a controlled-environment technological system.

name: School Garden
reason: Document says productive function warrants separate identification, but it overlaps the tool's existing schoolyard_greening typology.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration, with shade where fruit trees included

name: Market Garden
reason: Document's own note classes it as a production and business model; its intensive beds are already a listed component of the urban farm.

name: Edible Streetscape
reason: Edible species selection within an existing street system; the document directs its elements to Sections 2, A and B rather than redefining them.
cooling_mechanism: shade plus evapotranspiration - same as street planting

name: Productive Courtyard
reason: Document directs it to reference 3.5 Courtyard Greening for the spatial system; productive planting is a programme variant, not a new form.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration in a sheltered courtyard microclimate

name: Edible Park
reason: Target 4.18 was itself dropped: edible park duplicates the dropped productive park; food production is an attribute of a kept park, not a park typology.
resolution_note: Curation conflict resolved: originally proposed merge into 4.18, which is dropped.

name: Productive Greenhouse Landscape
reason: Document states a greenhouse alone is not an NbS; it is built agricultural infrastructure whose surroundings are covered by 8.1 and 8.5.
cooling_mechanism: none - enclosed structure, adds sensible heat

name: Agroforestry System
reason: Deliberate tree-plus-crop structure is a distinct physical form pairing canopy shade with cultivated ground; the canonical productive tree system.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade plus evapotranspiration from two layers

name: Urban Agroforestry
reason: Urban application of the same principles and forms already listed under 8.15; a context variant, not a separate physical typology.

name: Peri-urban Productive Landscape
reason: A location-defined land-use context, already captured by the tool's land_use and scale inputs; it is a package of 8.3, 8.4 and 8.15.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - regional cooling delivered by its components

name: Therapeutic Productive Garden
reason: Defined by therapeutic objective and user group, not by physical form; realised as a productive garden with accessible beds.

name: Community Orchard
reason: Document states explicitly that it is a governance subtype of 8.3 Urban Orchard.

name: Institutional Productive Garden
reason: A land-use context like hospital and campus landscape, captured by the tool's land_use input; physically it is 8.1 or 8.5 on institutional land.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - evapotranspiration via its components

name: Temporary Productive Landscape
reason: Defined by tenure and duration rather than form; a temporary condition modifying 8.1 or 8.5, which the document says limits tree planting and soil investment.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - reduced, no tree canopy

name: Productive Riparian Landscape
reason: Flood-compatible orchards and agroforestry sited in a riparian zone; a siting variant of 8.15, with the corridor itself covered by riparian_restoration.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade plus evapotranspiration near water

name: Green Infrastructure Network
reason: Document classes it as an infrastructure network, but it functions as the umbrella over 10.2-10.4; author may prefer only the specific networks.
cooling_mechanism: cumulative shade and evapotranspiration across connected spaces

name: Blue-Green Infrastructure Network
reason: Water storage and movement give it a spatial structure and cooling behaviour distinct from a vegetation-only network.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation and evapotranspiration from retained water

name: Urban Cooling Network
reason: Connected shaded routes and thermal refuges prioritised by heat exposure form a distinct district-scale spatial system; the core district entry for this tool.
cooling_mechanism: shade along routes plus evapotranspiration at refuges

name: Green Mobility Network
reason: Distinct substrate of walking, cycling and transit corridors, but its components and cooling behaviour overlap 10.3 substantially.
cooling_mechanism: shade over movement routes plus evapotranspiration

name: Sponge District
reason: Document states it is a district-wide water-management strategy, not one typology; it is a package of 10.2, rain gardens and floodable parks.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - evaporation via its components

name: Climate Adaptation District
reason: Document states it is a strategic district model, not a discrete landscape typology; it is a package of 10.1-10.3 plus building and productive entries.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - delivered by its components

name: Green Campus
reason: Document's note calls it an institutional spatial type; like campus landscape 3.8 it is a land-use context captured by the tool's land_use input.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - delivered by its components

name: Eco-district
reason: Document states an eco-district is not itself an NbS but a district-development model containing multiple NbS systems.

name: Biodiversity District
reason: Target 7.9 was itself dropped: biodiversity district duplicates the dropped ecological network; both are citywide strategies composed of kept corridors and cores.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from connected habitat, some canopy shade
resolution_note: Curation conflict resolved: originally proposed merge into 7.9, which is dropped.

name: Forest District
reason: Continuous district-wide canopy is a distinct physical structure with the strongest cooling, but it depends on the pending urban_forest ambiguity ruling.

name: Productive District
reason: District-scale coordination of Section 8 entries; the same umbrella logic that disqualified 8.6, and a package of 8.1, 8.3, 8.4 and C13.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - evapotranspiration via its components

name: Resilient Waterfront District
reason: A geographic context rather than a form; a package of riparian_restoration, living shorelines, floodable parks and blue-green streets.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - evaporation via its components

name: Climate-resilient Regeneration District
reason: Defined by delivery mode (retrofit of existing fabric) not physical form; a package of retrofitted street, courtyard, roof and park entries.
cooling_mechanism: none as an entry - delivered by its components

name: Extensive Green Roof
reason: Restates C1: lightweight shallow-substrate roof, stress-tolerant planting, maintenance-only access; identical functions and limitations.

name: Semi-intensive Green Roof
reason: Restates C2: intermediate substrate depth, grasses, perennials and small shrubs, partially accessible.

name: Intensive Green Roof
reason: Restates C3: deep substrate supporting lawns, shrubs and trees as a constructed landscape over a building.

name: Roof Garden
reason: Restates C4: accessible amenity-driven roof landscape; both warn a paved terrace with isolated planters is not equivalent.

name: Biodiverse Roof
reason: Restates C5 Biodiverse Green Roof: varied substrate depths, deadwood, mineral areas, habitat features; name shortened only.

name: Brown Roof
reason: Restates C6: nutrient-poor recycled mineral substrates recreating brownfield habitat; both warn it is not an unfinished roof.

name: Solar Green Roof
reason: Cross-references C12; same PV-plus-vegetation system, though 9.7 borrows C11's co-design language (see mismatch note).

name: Biosolar Roof
reason: Restates C11: energy production and biodiversity deliberately co-designed; both reject the label where vegetation is incidental.

name: Blue Roof
reason: Document binds it as non-NbS blue infrastructure or NbS-supporting component; duplicates C7, which carries the same disqualification.

name: Blue-green Roof
reason: Restates C8: vegetation combined with dedicated storage, water made available to plants by capillary action or irrigation.

name: Retention Green Roof
reason: Restates C9: defined rainfall volume retained in substrate or storage layers for plant use rather than delayed discharge.

name: Detention Green Roof
reason: Restates C10: vegetated roof delaying peak runoff through controlled temporary storage and release.

name: Productive Green Roof
reason: Restates C13 (and cross-refers 8.7): edible planting, herbs and small-scale horticulture on a roof.

name: Rooftop Farm
reason: Restates C14 at larger, managed scale; the conditional NbS test stated only here must be carried onto C14.

name: Roof Meadow
reason: Restates C15: grasses and flowering herbaceous species rather than sedum, with pollinator and seasonal diversity value.

name: Roof Wetland
reason: Restates C16: shallow water and wetland planting treating stormwater or greywater on a roof.

name: Rooftop Woodland or Tree Roof
reason: Restates C17: intensive roof carrying multiple trees and understory; both refuse equivalence with ground-based woodland.

name: Direct Ground-rooted Green Facade
reason: Restates D1: self-clinging climbers rooted in natural ground, attached directly to the wall, no support frame.
cooling_mechanism: shade and evapotranspiration on the wall surface

name: Indirect Ground-rooted Green Facade
reason: Restates D2: ground-rooted climbers on a separate support with an air gap in front of the facade.

name: Cable Facade
reason: Restates D3: tensioned cable system guiding climbers, suited to tall facades and narrow planting zones.

name: Mesh or Trellis Facade
reason: Restates D4: rigid or semi-rigid mesh, lattice or trellis giving denser support than cables.

name: Planter-rooted Green Facade
reason: Restates D5: climbers grown from containers at ground, intermediate floors, balconies or roof where soil is unavailable.

name: Cascading Facade Planting
reason: Restates D6: trailing plants growing downward from roof edges, balconies or facade-mounted planters.

name: Modular Living Wall
reason: Restates D7: vegetation in wall-mounted modules with integrated irrigation; same cost, failure-risk and value caveats.

name: Substrate-based Living Wall
reason: Restates D8: plants rooted in soil-like or engineered substrate held in modules, with greater buffering than hydroponics.

name: Hydroponic Living Wall
reason: Restates D9: soil-free wall fed by an engineered nutrient and irrigation system, highly dependent on mechanical plant.

name: Felt-pocket Living Wall
reason: Restates D10: plants in felt pockets, explicitly a subtype rather than a high-level category (parent differs, see note).

name: Vegetated Screen
reason: Restates D11: freestanding or facade-adjacent structure carrying climbers without forming part of the envelope.

name: Green Balcony
reason: No individual counterpart; a distinct building open-space element with substantial permanent planting, not merely D5 or D6 planters.

name: Green Terrace
reason: No individual counterpart; larger multi-layer planted terrace treated by the document as its own building open-space typology.

name: Green Atrium
reason: Document says it is not automatically an urban-cooling NbS; internal space with no outdoor microclimate effect unless conditions are met.

name: Vegetated Building Courtyard
reason: Self-declared cross-reference to 3.5 Courtyard Greening, already a tool typology; building scale adds no distinct physical form.

name: Green Podium
reason: No individual counterpart; landscape over podium or parking structure with pedestrian-level, semi-public cooling unlike any roof entry.

name: Vegetated Pergola Attached to a Building
reason: Cross-references E1-E2; a building-attached instance of the green pergola element, not a separate typology.

name: Green Building Envelope
reason: Self-declared coordinated building-level strategy, not a physical typology; a package of kept roof, facade, balcony and courtyard entries.
cooling_mechanism: none in itself; inherited from component elements

name: Building-integrated Habitat System
reason: Biodiversity objective bundling C5, facades and nesting features; a package of kept entries, not a discrete intervention.
cooling_mechanism: none in itself; inherited from component elements

name: Building-integrated Water and Vegetation System
reason: Water-circulation strategy linking C8/C9 roofs, facades and ground bioretention; a package of kept entries, not a typology.
cooling_mechanism: none in itself; inherited from component elements
